name: Powerica Ltd
title: Powerica Ltd - 544744 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Powerica Q2 FY27 revenue INR847 crore with 15.2% EBITDA margin; fresh steel, copper and aluminium inflation puts further price hikes on the table.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue was about INR847-848 crore, with reported EBITDA of about INR128 crore (15.2% margin) and PAT of about INR71 crore (8.4% margin), improving sequentially as earlier price revisions flowed through. H1 FY27 revenue was INR1,628 crore (up 12.5% YoY), with EBITDA margin of 14.4% and PAT margin of 8.3%. Management said a fresh round of raw-material inflation (steel, then copper and aluminium) since Q3 began means earlier price hikes have not fully offset input costs, so further calibrated hikes are planned. The company reiterated double-digit revenue growth guidance for FY27.

segments.name: DG sets (Cummins-powered gensets)
segments.commentary: Drove Q2 growth with 14% YoY increase; about 80.6% of H1 revenue at 6.5% EBITDA margin. Data centres were about 20% of H1 revenue; medium and high horsepower demand strong, low horsepower price-competitive.

segments.name: DG sets (Hyundai-powered) and MSLG
segments.commentary: Project-linked and muted: MSLG revenue INR16 crore in H1 FY27 vs INR74 crore a year earlier, delayed by Middle East conflict, including an attack in Saudi Arabia.

segments.name: Allied business (defence, Schneider, projects)
segments.commentary: H1 down about 6% YoY; defence orders deliberately slowed on margin and working-capital grounds, while Prisma panel for Schneider and large data centre projects grew steadily, with revenue timing dependent on client certification.

segments.name: Wind power (IPP and EPC)
segments.commentary: Contributed 19.4% of H1 revenue at 47.4% EBITDA margin. About 330 MW operational, 50 MW under construction, plus 250 MW newly won in reverse auctions. New LoI for 50 MW GUVNL project at INR3.51/kWh over 25 years.

guidance_outlook: Double-digit revenue growth reiterated for FY27 despite near-term margin pressure.
Further very calibrated price hikes planned in Q3 FY27 as new steel price increases came through in October; some RM moderation expected if geopolitical conditions improve.
Management said current pricing covers inflation as it stands, with price changes monitored almost daily; no further hikes needed if raw materials stabilise.
Steady-state margins per management: genset about 9% consolidated; wind IPP blended 60-65% (average 62%), new projects 82-85%; EPC about 10%.
Wind capacity target 638 MW within about 2.5 years, then adding 100-150 MW a year; long-term ambition of 1 GW in wind and renewables.
capex_capacity: Wind: about 330 MW operational; 50 MW under construction, expected to complete soon; 250 MW newly won (GUVNL 100+ MW with machinery arriving, GUVNL 50+ MW and SECI 100 MW with land procurement under way).
Wind project timelines: 24 months from PPA signing; company says it has historically commissioned ahead of schedule.
Funding: first-phase wind expansion to be about 70% debt-funded; company is at near zero debt post-IPO for its 330 MW wind business.
EPC: about 450 MW completed for other customers and about 600 MW in hand for group and other companies.
Joint development JV with GE Vernova signed; announcement expected for GE projects.
demand_pricing: DG order book INR1,950 crore as of October 2026, with about INR1,200 crore data centre and the balance (about INR750 crore) short-cycle orders from manufacturing, real estate, rental and infrastructure; the large order book is to execute over 12-18 months.
Demand described as strong in medium and high horsepower; low horsepower price-competitive with more players; no new major entrants reported in HHP (QSK).
Infrastructure growing moderately; manufacturing remains the largest contributor by segment.
Price revisions: more revisions in the past six months than in the prior three to four years; pass-through lags because the pending order book is a mix of old and new prices.
Procurement: bulk buying and inventory timing based on market intelligence to manage input costs.

qa_highlights.question: How much did data centres contribute to H1 revenue, and how much will execute in H2?
qa_highlights.answer: Data centres were about 20% of H1 revenue; H2 execution is hard to quantify because it depends on site readiness, though a healthy contribution is expected.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the pricing benefit came in Q2 and how much is still to come?
qa_highlights.answer: Not quantifiable: existing and new orders flow through in a mix. Margin improvement expected, with further calibrated hikes on new orders.

qa_highlights.question: What price hike was taken in gensets and what are steady-state margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Price hikes are set at a detailed level so no single figure given. Steady state: genset about 9%, wind IPP 60-65% blended, EPC about 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Does current pricing cover RM inflation, and will margins normalise within two quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said current pricing covers inflation as it stands. Normalisation may not take two quarters because non-data-centre orders cycle in two days to six months, but pass-on lag has grown with continued commodity rises.

qa_highlights.question: Why is ex-data-centre order book flat and is competition rising?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no new competitors and competition is unchanged from the past two years; ex-data-centre demand is growing steadily.

qa_highlights.question: Allied business down 6% in H1 and MSLG L1 order status?
qa_highlights.answer: Defence orders slowed on margin and inflation grounds; MSLG L1 order on hold due to the Middle East situation, with restart expected in about 1-2 months. A INR41 crore PSU pilot order is due late Q4 or early Q1 FY28.

qa_highlights.question: Wind capacity roadmap and long-term economics?
qa_highlights.answer: Target 638 MW, then 100-150 MW added a year toward 1 GW; new projects earn 82-85% EBITDA, blended 62-65% now, expected to rise to 72-73%.

risks_watch: Steel, copper and aluminium inflation since Q3 FY27 not fully offset; margin recovery depends on further price hikes and pass-through timing.
Middle East conflict delaying MSLG and Hyundai-engine project revenue, including the L1 order.
Data centre execution timing depends on customer site readiness, not Powerica supply; H2 contribution not quantified.
Low horsepower segment price competition; high horsepower competition currently limited.
Infrastructure growing only moderately; defence orders deliberately slowed.
Wind project execution against 24-month timelines and the 70% debt funding plan for the expansion.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and the double-digit growth guidance, but cautious on margins, which management says are still under pressure from fresh raw-material inflation. Management was evasive when asked to quantify pricing pass-through, data-centre H2 execution and the price hike size, citing volatility and customer timing.
key_quotes: Despite the near-term challenges, we remain confident about our growth outlook and continue to expect double-digit revenue growth through financial year 2027.
Effectively, earlier price increases have not fully offset the sharp rise in input costs.
We've made more revisions in the past six months than we probably have over the past, like, three to four years, just because of the volatility.
So, we are very firm in terms of the growth guidance that we have given double-digit growth.

growth.why: Double-digit FY27 revenue growth reiterated, backed by a INR1,950 crore DG order book (about INR1,200 crore data centre, executing over 12-18 months), 50 MW wind under construction and 250 MW newly won; H1 revenue was up 12.5% YoY, but the quarterly YoY growth and the 10% figure are only the floor of double-digit guidance, and the 250 MW wind additions lack firm commissioning dates.

quality.why: Q2 growth was led by the DG set (genset) business, up 14% YoY on strong medium and high horsepower demand and a INR1,950 crore order book (about INR1,200 crore data centre), while MSLG and allied (defence) were weak; the brief cites no acquisition or one-off item, so growth looks recurring, though the brief does not split volume from price.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 FY27 EBITDA margin 15.2% and H1 14.4%, but fresh steel, copper and aluminium inflation is not fully offset; management expects further calibrated hikes in Q3 FY27 and says normalisation may take longer than two quarters, while steady-state genset margin is about 9% and wind IPP blended 60-65%.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: About 50 MW wind under construction is expected to complete soon, and 250 MW newly won in reverse auctions (GUVNL 100+ MW with machinery arriving) is in progress; wind timelines are 24 months from PPA with a history of early commissioning.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: H1 FY27 revenue up 12.5% YoY, Q2 genset up 14% YoY, and a INR1,950 crore DG order book (about INR1,200 crore data centre) executes over 12-18 months, though the data-centre H2 contribution is not quantified.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Wind target of 638 MW within about 2.5 years then 100-150 MW a year toward 1 GW, with first-phase expansion about 70% debt-funded and the company near zero debt post-IPO; land procurement for GUVNL 50+ MW and SECI 100 MW is under way and the GE Vernova JV announcement is expected.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management reiterated only double-digit FY27 revenue growth and said margins are still under pressure from fresh raw-material inflation, with no upgrade flagged.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: MSLG revenue fell to INR16 crore in H1 FY27 from INR74 crore a year earlier on the Middle East conflict, defence orders were deliberately slowed (Allied down about 6% in H1), and raw-material pass-through lags.

rows.label: Data centre DG execution over 12-18 months
rows.why: INR1,200 crore of the INR1,950 crore DG order book is data centre, about 20% of H1 revenue, but H2 timing depends on customer site readiness and is not quantified.

rows.label: MSLG L1 order restart and PSU pilot order
rows.why: MSLG L1 order is on hold due to the Middle East situation with restart expected in 1-2 months, and a INR41 crore PSU pilot order is due late Q4 or early Q1 FY28.

rows.label: Further calibrated price hikes in Q3 FY27
rows.why: New steel price increases in October are not fully offset by earlier hikes, and management plans further very calibrated hikes on new orders, though size was not quantified.

tone.note: Management was confident on demand, data-centre orders and double-digit FY27 growth but cautious on margins under fresh steel, copper and aluminium inflation; analysts pressed on pricing pass-through, H2 data-centre execution and margin normalisation timing, which management largely declined to quan
